nodes.name: In situ Chemical Bath Deposition
nodes.procedure: N–NiFe LDH film was prepared by a facile one-step chemical bath deposition (CBD) method using nickel and iron salts as precursors, hexamethylenetetramine (HMT, C6H12N4) as both the structural template and nitrogen source, and nickel foam as a substrate.
nodes.source_text: N–NiFe LDH film was prepared by a facile one-step chemical bath deposition (CBD) method using nickel and iron salts as precursors, hexamethylenetetramine (HMT, C6H12N4) as both the structural template and nitrogen source, and nickel foam as a substrate (see the Experimental section, Supporting Information for details)... The material is synthesized by a facile CBD method under mild condition, i.e., 60 °C, 1 atm, and in a beaker

N–NiFe LDH has demonstrated an excellent OER catalytic activity with a small onset overpotential of 0.21 V... η₁₀ of 0.23 V... Tafel slope of 35 mV dec⁻¹... A 60 h chronoamperometric test of N–NiFe LDH shows a seldom attenuation in current density
Negligible change in current density from 0 to 1 V indicates a desirable four-electron pathway... low fraction of HO₂⁻ (<2 %) and high electron transfer number (3.92–3.95)

Faradaic efficiency was studied on RRDE by imposing a negative overpotential (-0.566 V vs Ag/AgCl) on Pt ring electrode to reduce the O₂ generated by disk electrode (≈200 μA). A high Faradaic efficiency of ≈98 % was obtained

A slow linear scan of 5 mV s⁻¹ was performed from 0 to 1 V in O₂-saturated alkaline electrolyte. As seen in Figure 3A, the pristine color of N–NiFe LDH electrode is gray silver, which tunes to dark black during OER process... persist for at least 5000 cycles

The battery can work smoothly with an open circuit of 1.27 V... discharge at different current densities such as 1.24 V at 0.1 mA cm⁻², 1.16 V at 0.2 mA cm⁻², and 1.12 V at 0.3 mA cm⁻². The peak power density was 0.55 mW cm⁻² at 0.65 V

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show 3D microporous film composed of numerous thin nanolayers vertically grown on nickel foam framework.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The resultant material is a 3D microporous film composed of numerous thin nanolayers vertically grown on the framework (Figure 1 A–C).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images show nanolayers with several hundred nanometers size and well-crystallized layered structure; SAED reveals polycrystalline structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nanolayers have several hundred nanometers size (Figure 1 D–F) with well-crystallized layered structure (Figure 1 E). Selected area electron diffraction (SAED) reveals that individual nanosheet is polycrystalline in structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM determines nanolayer thickness as ≈0.8 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the thickness of nanolayers has been determined by atomic force microscopy (AFM) as ≈0.8 nm (Figure 1 G and Figure S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Element mappings show homogeneous distribution of Ni and Fe throughout the whole region; contains Ni, Fe, O, and N as main components.
nodes.evidence_snippet: N–NiFe LDH contains Ni, Fe, O, and N as the main components (Figure 1 H and Figure S2, Supporting Information), and element mappings show a homogeneous distribution of Ni and Fe throughout the whole region (Figure 1 C,F).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS reveals N-doping ratio of ≈17.8%; Ni and Fe have oxidation states of +2 and +3; stoichiometric molar ratio N:Ni:Fe:O is 0.76:1:0.51:2.02.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis reveals that the doping ratio was as high as ≈17.8% for N in N–NiFe LDH (Figure 1 H).

nodes.characterization_summary: All Bragg reflections match well with typical structural profile of LDH materials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: These results are consistent with X-ray diffraction (XRD, Figure S3, Supporting Information), where all Bragg reflections match well with the typical structural profile of LDH materials.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra display two remarkable peaks around 470 and 569 cm^{-1} attributable to Ni-O bending and stretching vibrations of NiFe LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, Raman spectra (Figure S4, Supporting Information) display two remarkable peaks around 470 and 569 cm^{-1} that are attributable to the Ni-O bending and stretching vibrations of NiFe LDH.
